title: As Marijuana’s Popularity Grows, So Do Its Harms

sentences.zh: 我曾在凌晨4点半给总统打电话，他接听了。

sentences.zh: 七十年的太空探索。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗恒星之外有什么。

sentences.zh: 今天我正在测试七款床垫。

sentences.en: 60 super sundaes.

sentences.en: The New York Times, celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》，庆祝175年来致力于帮助您了解世界并充分利用每一天。

sentences.en: Subscribe now for a special offer at nytimes.com slash subscribe.
sentences.zh: 立即订阅，获取nytimes.com/subscribe上的特别优惠。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Rachel Abrams, and this is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的Rachel Abrams，这是《每日简报》。

sentences.en: This election day, recreational marijuana could become legal across more than half of the United States.
sentences.zh: 在这个选举日，娱乐用大麻可能在美国超过半数的州实现合法化。

sentences.en: But as more Americans consume more potent forms of the drug more often, a Times investigation has revealed that some of the heaviest users
sentences.zh: 但随着越来越多的美国人更频繁地使用效力更强的大麻产品，《纽约时报》的一项调查显示，一些重度使用者

sentences.en: are experiencing serious and unexpected harms to their health.
sentences.zh: 正在经历严重且意想不到的健康损害。

sentences.en: Today, I spoke with my colleague, investigative reporter Megan Toohey, about what she found.
sentences.zh: 今天，我与我的同事、调查记者Megan Toohey聊了聊她的发现。

sentences.en: It's Tuesday, October 22nd.
sentences.zh: 今天是10月22日，星期二。

sentences.en: Hi, Megan.
sentences.zh: 你好，Megan。

sentences.en: Hey, Rachel.
sentences.zh: 嘿，Rachel。

sentences.en: Thank you for being here.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你来到这里。

sentences.en: So, Megan, today we're going to talk about something that a lot of people, myself included, have at least a glancing familiarity with, and that's marijuana.
sentences.zh: Megan，今天我们要聊一个很多人（包括我自己）至少都有所耳闻的话题，那就是大麻。

sentences.en: So tell me, first of all, how did you come to this story?
sentences.zh: 那么首先告诉我，你是怎么接触到这个故事的？

sentences.en: Well, full disclosure, I am one of those people who has some familiarity with marijuana.
sentences.zh: 好吧，坦白说，我就是那些对大麻有所了解的人之一。

sentences.en: I have dabbled in it on and off, stretching back to the 1990s.
sentences.zh: 从20世纪90年代开始，我就断断续续地尝试过。

sentences.en: And so I, as a consumer, have also been among those who have noticed the drastic transformation
sentences.zh: 所以作为一名消费者，我也注意到近年来随着合法化的普及，以及商业化合法产业的兴起并开始提供各种产品，

sentences.en: of marijuana in this country in recent years as legalization spread and the commercialized legal industry sprung up and began offering products.
sentences.zh: 大麻在这个国家发生了巨大的转变。

sentences.en: And so, you know, here in New York, a couple years ago, when we implemented the legalization
sentences.zh: 你知道，几年前我们在纽约实施了娱乐用大麻合法化，

sentences.en: of recreational marijuana, there was sort of all of a sudden a dispensary selling products on nearly, like, every corner.
sentences.zh: 几乎每个街角突然间就冒出了一家销售大麻产品的药房。

sentences.en: Everywhere.
sentences.zh: 到处都是。

sentences.en: Everywhere.
sentences.zh: 到处都是。

sentences.en: And so I was one of the people who started going into the dispensaries and immediately noticed
sentences.zh: 于是我开始走进这些药房，并立刻注意到

sentences.en: that the products I was seeing there were very different from some of the products I had consumed.
sentences.zh: 我在那里看到的产品与我过去使用过的一些产品非常不同。

sentences.en: And, you know, there were pre-rolled joints and gummies and these, like, almost pure concentrates of THC, which is the intoxicating component of marijuana.
sentences.zh: 你知道，有预卷好的大麻烟、软糖，还有几乎是纯THC的浓缩物，THC是大麻中致幻的成分。

sentences.en: And so I could see for the first time that there was a huge range and that there were products that had, like, really, really high levels of THC.
sentences.zh: 所以我第一次意识到，产品种类非常丰富，而且有些产品的THC含量真的非常、非常高。

sentences.en: And so I would purchase these little containers of gummies that contain five milligrams of THC, which is on the very low end.
sentences.zh: 我会购买那些含有5毫克THC的小盒软糖，这属于非常低的剂量。

sentences.en: But when I would go home and take little bites of them, in my experience, they were actually quite strong and were being framed as completely almost innocuous.
sentences.zh: 但当我回家吃一点点时，以我的经验，它们其实相当强劲，却被包装得几乎完全无害。

sentences.en: You know, I have to tell you, I've also had kind of a hard time navigating this market and these shops that are for recreational use.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我不得不告诉你，我在浏览这个市场和这些娱乐用大麻商店时也感到很困难。

sentences.en: But you can also go in and you can say something like, I have a headache or I have trouble sleeping.
sentences.zh: 你可以走进去说，比如我头痛或者睡眠不好。

sentences.en: And somebody who is not a doctor, is not a pharmacist, is suddenly recommending a product to you to help you with your health issue.
sentences.zh: 然后一个既不是医生也不是药剂师的人，突然就会向你推荐一种产品来帮助你解决健康问题。

sentences.en: Well, I think you make a really good point, Rachel, which is that legalization of marijuana began as the legalization of medical marijuana in this country.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我觉得你提到了一个很好的观点，Rachel，那就是大麻合法化在这个国家最初是以医用大麻合法化的形式开始的。

sentences.en: I mean, the first states to legalize did that for the purposes of people being able to use it for health reasons.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，最早实现合法化的州，其目的都是为了让人们能够出于健康原因使用它。

sentences.en: But what we have seen in the last 10 years is that what began as a medical marijuana market has been superseded by a recreational marijuana market.
sentences.zh: 但在过去10年里，我们看到的是，最初的医用大麻市场已经被娱乐用大麻市场所取代。

sentences.en: And, you know, the promise of legalization was that it was going to make marijuana more safe.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，合法化的承诺是让大麻变得更安全。

sentences.en: That with legalization, you'd have regulation and oversight and more protection of consumers.
sentences.zh: 通过合法化，你可以拥有监管、监督以及对消费者更多的保护。

sentences.en: But there's now a $33 billion industry that sprung up to deliver these products in this newly legal market.
sentences.zh: 但现在，一个价值330亿美元的产业已经兴起，专门在这个新合法化的市场中提供这些产品。

sentences.en: And the products that they're delivering are at potency levels that were almost unimaginable a generation ago.
sentences.zh: 而他们提供的产品，其效力水平在上一代人看来几乎是不可想象的。

sentences.en: And I knew from not just my own personal experience of interfacing with the commercial market, but
sentences.zh: 而且我不仅从自己与商业市场打交道的个人经验中了解到这一点，

sentences.en: also from people in my life and in my various, like, orbits, I was hearing about people who were actually struggling with marijuana.
sentences.zh: 还从我生活圈子里的其他人那里听说，有些人确实在大麻问题上挣扎。

sentences.en: And those folks and their families had a lot of confusion.
sentences.zh: 那些人和他们的家人感到非常困惑。

sentences.en: Like, what isn't this supposed to be this totally safe and totally natural and now totally legal drug?
sentences.zh: 比如，这难道不是一种完全安全、完全天然，而且现在完全合法的大麻吗？

sentences.en: And it just felt like there was a real vacuum of information.
sentences.zh: 感觉信息真的非常匮乏。

sentences.en: So what did you do just to start trying to understand this world that's obviously confusing a lot of people?
sentences.zh: 那么，为了开始了解这个显然让很多人感到困惑的世界，你做了什么？

sentences.en: So with that kind of initial interest, I just started to make some phone calls.
sentences.zh: 带着最初的那种兴趣，我开始打一些电话。

sentences.en: And one of the first people I called was a longtime medical marijuana researcher who helped develop
sentences.zh: 我打给的第一批人中，有一位资深的医用大麻研究员，他曾参与开发

sentences.en: a couple of the only pharmaceutical drugs that have cannabis components that have received regulatory approval.
sentences.zh: 仅有的几种获得监管批准的含有大麻成分的药物。

sentences.en: Interestingly enough, one of the first things he said to me was, oh, my God, good luck reporting into this.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，他对我说的第一句话就是：天哪，祝你报道这个好运。

sentences.en: It's like a total jungle.
sentences.zh: 这简直是一片丛林。

sentences.en: Well, I've been in this world for decades, and even I have a hard time following exactly what's going on because so much has been shifting so faSt.
sentences.zh: 我在这个领域待了几十年，连我有时都很难跟上到底发生了什么，因为变化实在太快了。

sentences.en: And so that was a little scary to hear, but also intriguing.
sentences.zh: 听到这些有点吓人，但也很有吸引力。

sentences.en: And one of the things that he said was that he had major concerns with the way that legalization and commercialization of marijuana was playing out here in the United States.
sentences.zh: 他说的其中一件事是，他对美国大麻合法化和商业化的发展方式有重大担忧。

sentences.en: He said that scientists and researchers and doctors like himself were on the sidelines, that
sentences.zh: 他说，像他这样的科学家、研究人员和医生都被边缘化了，

sentences.en: they weren't being consulted as this was rolling out, and that the industry that had sprung up,
sentences.zh: 在政策推行时没有咨询他们的意见，而且那个兴起的产业，

sentences.en: this $33 billion industry, was also not focused on the therapeutic products of the drug, but instead had basically ended up in a race to produce the most potent products, the most
sentences.zh: 这个330亿美元的产业，也没有专注于药物的治疗作用，而是基本上陷入了一场竞赛，竞相生产效力最强、

sentences.en: intoxicating products possible.
sentences.zh: 致幻效果最强的产品。

sentences.en: And what I next realized was that there was a real dearth of research, of scientific research, into the effects of marijuana.
sentences.zh: 我接下来意识到的是，关于大麻影响的科学研究确实非常匮乏。

sentences.en: And that's in part because while marijuana is now legal in about half the states, it has remained illegal at the federal level.
sentences.zh: 这部分是因为虽然大麻现在在约半数的州合法，但在联邦层面它仍然是非法的。

sentences.en: And it's also in this highly restrictive category of drug, which makes it really challenging for people to do research on it.
sentences.zh: 而且它还处于一种限制极高的药物类别中，这使得人们进行相关研究变得非常困难。

sentences.en: Also, the hospital and other health care data on the effects of marijuana was really inadequate.
sentences.zh: 此外，医院和其他医疗机构关于大麻影响的数据也非常不足。

sentences.en: And the patchwork of state laws that had sprung up to govern this was not equipped to do any meaningful tracking of the health outcomes.
sentences.zh: 而为了管理这一现状而建立的各州法律拼凑在一起，根本无法对健康结果进行任何有意义的追踪。

sentences.en: And so after a while, I realized that if we really wanted to have a deeper understanding of how this
sentences.zh: 所以过了一段时间，我意识到如果我们真的想深入了解这种

sentences.en: drug was affecting consumers across the country, we were going to have to figure out ways to gather that information ourselves.
sentences.zh: 药物是如何影响全国消费者的，我们就必须想办法自己收集这些信息。

sentences.en: I was lucky enough to, at this point, be joined by two of my colleagues on the investigations team,
sentences.zh: 我很幸运，此时调查团队的两位同事加入了我的行列，

sentences.en: Danielle Ivory and Carson Kessler.
sentences.zh: Danielle Ivory和Carson Kessler。

sentences.en: And one of the first things that we sought to tackle was this data set on drug use in this country.
sentences.zh: 我们试图解决的第一件事就是这个关于全国药物使用的数据集。

sentences.en: Every year, the government does a population survey that asks Americans about their use of drugs
sentences.zh: 政府每年都会进行一项人口调查，询问美国人关于他们使用药物的情况，

sentences.en: drugs and how frequently they use it and seeks to measure the effect on their lives.
sentences.zh: 以及他们使用的频率，并试图衡量其对他们生活的影响。

sentences.en: And mostly what people have focused on are opioids, because historically, those drugs have killed the most people and done the most harm.
sentences.zh: 人们主要关注的是阿片类药物，因为从历史上看，这些药物致死人数最多，造成的伤害也最大。

sentences.en: So what this survey has shown on marijuana use hasn't received a ton of attention.
sentences.zh: 所以这项调查显示的大麻使用情况并没有受到太多关注。

sentences.en: It's sort of been flying under the radar.
sentences.zh: 它一直处于被忽视的状态。

sentences.en: But we found a researcher at Columbia University who has looked at this data and looked at specifically at marijuana.
sentences.zh: 但我们在哥伦比亚大学找到了一位研究员，她查看了这些数据，并专门研究了大麻。

sentences.en: And we asked her to do a more detailed analysis of those responses for us.
sentences.zh: 我们请她为我们对这些回复进行了更详细的分析。

sentences.en: And what did that analysis find?
sentences.zh: 那项分析发现了什么？

sentences.en: Well, the survey has turned up some very interesting trends with regards to marijuana use in this
sentences.zh: 嗯，这项调查揭示了一些关于大麻使用方面非常有趣的趋势。

sentences.en: country, it has shown that as legalization and commercialization of marijuana has taken off and accelerated, that marijuana use has been going up steadily among people 18 and over.
sentences.zh: 它显示，随着大麻合法化和商业化的兴起并加速，18岁及以上人群的大麻使用量一直在稳步上升。

sentences.en: And it's not just that more people are consuming here and there.
sentences.zh: 而且不仅仅是更多的人偶尔使用。

sentences.en: There are pretty sharp rising rates of people who are using it on a daily or near daily basis.
sentences.zh: 每天或几乎每天使用的人数比例正在急剧上升。

sentences.en: And this survey showed that in 2022, in fact, for the very first time, more people said that
sentences.zh: 这项调查显示，事实上在2022年，这是第一次，更多的人表示

sentences.en: they were using marijuana on a daily or near daily basis than said they were using alcohol.
sentences.zh: 他们每天或几乎每天使用大麻，而不是使用酒精。

sentences.en: But not only are people using marijuana at higher rates than ever before, more people are reporting that their marijuana use is having a negative impact on their lives.
sentences.zh: 不仅人们使用大麻的频率比以往任何时候都高，更多的人报告说他们的大麻使用对生活产生了负面影响。

sentences.en: And this is more broadly known as cannabis use disorder.
sentences.zh: 这在更广泛的意义上被称为大麻使用障碍。

sentences.en: There's 11 specific criteria that are used to measure whether or not somebody is having like a problematic use of a drug.
sentences.zh: 有11项具体标准用于衡量某人是否对药物存在问题使用。

sentences.en: And, you know, it ranges from like building up tolerance to craving the drug to not being able to stop even if it's having negative effects on your social life or your job.
sentences.zh: 你知道，范围从产生耐受性、对药物产生渴望，到即使对社交生活或工作产生负面影响也无法停止使用。

sentences.en: And, you know, if you meet two of the criteria, then you are considered to have a mild case of cannabis use disorder.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，如果你符合其中两项标准，那么你就被认为患有轻度大麻使用障碍。

sentences.en: And then on the far end, if you meet six or more criteria, then you are considered to have a severe cannabis use disorder, widely seen as addiction.
sentences.zh: 而在另一端，如果你符合六项或更多标准，那么你被认为患有严重的大麻使用障碍，这被广泛视为成瘾。

sentences.en: And what this analysis showed was that 30 percent of cannabis users 18 and over reported having some level of cannabis use disorder.
sentences.zh: 这项分析显示，30%的18岁及以上大麻使用者报告称患有某种程度的大麻使用障碍。

sentences.en: That's like an estimated 18 million Americans.
sentences.zh: 这估计有1800万美国人。

sentences.en: And of those, about 3 million people are considered addicted.
sentences.zh: 其中，约300万人被认为已经成瘾。

sentences.en: I have to say, I was really surprised to hear that, that people could be addicted to marijuana.
sentences.zh: 我不得不说，听到这个我真的很惊讶，人们竟然会对大麻上瘾。

sentences.en: And frankly, I guess I was like a little skeptical when we were discussing and planning this episode.
sentences.zh: 坦白说，我想我们在讨论和策划这一集时，我还有点怀疑。

sentences.en: And it actually prompted a whole discussion here at The Daily about this, where people were saying, you know, actually, I know this one person who has an addiction problem.
sentences.zh: 这实际上引发了我们在《每日简报》内部的一场讨论，大家都在说，你知道，其实我认识某个人就有成瘾问题。

sentences.en: I know this other person who has an addiction problem.
sentences.zh: 我认识另一个人也有成瘾问题。

sentences.en: It was really, at least for me, it was really quite eye-opening.
sentences.zh: 这对我来说，确实非常令人大开眼界。

sentences.en: Yeah, listen, I think that there has long been this belief that marijuana is not addictive.
sentences.zh: 是的，听着，我认为长期以来人们一直认为大麻不会让人上瘾。

sentences.en: And I think that that's in large part because it presents differently than, say, alcohol addiction
sentences.zh: 我认为这在很大程度上是因为它的表现形式与酒精成瘾不同，

sentences.en: or opioid addiction, for which withdrawal can sometimes be so severe that it can be fatal.
sentences.zh: 或者与阿片类药物成瘾不同，后者的戒断反应有时非常严重，甚至可能致命。

sentences.en: But in recent years, medical experts have been able to show how when our systems are basically overrun with THC, you need more and more to get the same effect.
sentences.zh: 但近年来，医学专家已经能够证明，当我们的系统基本上被THC淹没时，你需要越来越多的量才能达到同样的效果。

sentences.en: And when you stop using, you can experience anxiety, depression, and other symptoms of withdrawal.
sentences.zh: 当你停止使用时，你可能会经历焦虑、抑郁和其他戒断症状。

sentences.en: So what else did you find in your analysis of the data?
sentences.zh: 那么你在数据分析中还发现了什么？

sentences.en: We found that this problematic use of marijuana is, you know, really stark among young people.
sentences.zh: 我们发现这种大麻的问题使用在年轻人中非常明显。

sentences.en: Like in the 18 to 25-year-old group, 4.5 million of them use marijuana daily or near daily.
sentences.zh: 比如在18到25岁的群体中，有450万人每天或几乎每天使用大麻。

sentences.en: And of those, 81 percent meet the criteria of cannabis use disorder in some way.
sentences.zh: 其中，81%的人在某种程度上符合大麻使用障碍的标准。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So basically, millions of young people are using marijuana every day.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，数百万年轻人每天都在使用大麻。

sentences.en: And a huge percentage of them are reporting problems with it.
sentences.zh: 而且其中很大一部分人报告说因此遇到了问题。

sentences.en: So, I mean, doesn't that seem like a clear warning sign?
sentences.zh: 所以，这难道看起来不像是一个明确的警告信号吗？

sentences.en: Yes, like for sure.
sentences.zh: 是的，当然是。

sentences.en: Now, I should say the vast majority of people who use just general users of marijuana are not having problems with it.
sentences.zh: 现在，我应该说，绝大多数使用大麻的普通用户并没有遇到问题。

sentences.en: But we wanted to learn more about those who were.
sentences.zh: 但我们想更多地了解那些遇到问题的人。

sentences.en: And when we started gathering more information, we were surprised by just how severe some of those issues could get.
sentences.zh: 当我们开始收集更多信息时，我们惊讶地发现其中一些问题可能变得多么严重。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由像你刚才听到的人们制作的。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 前往nytimes.com/games开始游戏吧。

sentences.en: Okay, so what kind of problems were chronic users reporting?
sentences.zh: 好的，那么长期使用者报告了哪些类型的问题？

sentences.en: Well, there were actually a couple of issues that we heard about.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们确实听到了一些问题。

sentences.en: And to get a clearer picture of them and understand how common they were, we started crafting a bunch of surveys.
sentences.zh: 为了更清楚地了解它们并弄清它们有多普遍，我们开始制作一系列调查问卷。

sentences.en: And we posted them in a Facebook group where people had come together to discuss one of these severe health effects from marijuana.
sentences.zh: 我们把它们发布在一个Facebook群组里，那里的人们聚在一起讨论大麻带来的这些严重健康影响之一。

sentences.en: And we also sent out surveys to doctors from a variety of fields across the country asking what they were seeing with their patients.
sentences.zh: 我们还向全国各地的医生发送了调查问卷，询问他们在病人身上看到了什么。

sentences.en: And we started to see some really concerning issues again and again.
sentences.zh: 我们开始一次又一次地看到一些非常令人担忧的问题。

sentences.en: Like what?
sentences.zh: 比如什么？

sentences.en: Well, let me tell you about one woman we met.
sentences.zh: 嗯，让我给你讲讲我们遇到的一位女士。

sentences.en: Hello.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: Hi, is this Jennifer?
sentences.zh: 你好，是Jennifer吗？

sentences.en: Yes, it is.
sentences.zh: 是的，我是。

sentences.en: Hi, this is Danielle.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是Danielle。

sentences.en: Her name is Jennifer Macaluso.
sentences.zh: 她的名字叫Jennifer Macaluso。

sentences.en: She's from Illinois.
sentences.zh: 她来自伊利诺伊州。

sentences.en: And my colleague, Danielle Ivory, spoke to her over the phone.
sentences.zh: 我的同事Danielle Ivory通过电话与她进行了交谈。

sentences.en: Is this still a good time for you to talk?
sentences.zh: 现在方便通话吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, this is great.
sentences.zh: 是的，很方便。

sentences.en: All right, excellent.
sentences.zh: 好的，太棒了。

sentences.en: And in a way, Jennifer is a great example of a kind of person who started using weed post-legalization.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，Jennifer是一个很好的例子，代表了那种在合法化后开始使用大麻的人。

sentences.en: You know, I'm 51.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我51岁了。

sentences.en: I used cannabis briefly when I was a teenager, like a lot of kids do.
sentences.zh: 我十几岁时曾短暂使用过大麻，就像很多孩子那样。

sentences.en: You know, I wasn't addicted.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我没有上瘾。

sentences.en: You know, nothing.
sentences.zh: 你知道，什么都没有。

sentences.en: It was social, whatever.
sentences.zh: 那只是社交，随便玩玩。

sentences.en: You know, she had smoked when she was a teen, but nothing very serious and had actually stopped as an adult until she got a bit older.
sentences.zh: 你知道，她十几岁时抽过，但没什么严重的，成年后实际上已经停止了，直到她年纪大了一些。

sentences.en: In 2019, I started having some other health probleMs.
sentences.zh: 2019年，我开始出现一些其他的健康问题。

sentences.en: She got migraines.
sentences.zh: 她开始偏头痛。

sentences.en: And she took a lot of medication to get them under control.
sentences.zh: 为了控制病情，她服用了大量的药物。

sentences.en: Here I am popping pills every day just to function.
sentences.zh: 我每天都要靠吃药才能维持正常生活。

sentences.en: So my doctor at the time suggested, what about medical marijuana?
sentences.zh: 当时我的医生建议，要不要试试医用大麻？

sentences.en: It had become legal in our state a few years prior.
sentences.zh: 几年前，大麻在我们州已经合法化了。

sentences.en: And, you know, I thought, wow, OK, yeah.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我当时想，哇，好吧，行。

sentences.en: You know, I'm always one for a more natural route.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我一直倾向于更自然的方法。

sentences.en: I juSt...
sentences.zh: 我只是……

sentences.en: So she started using weed on the recommendation of her doctor to help with the headaches.
sentences.zh: 于是，在医生的建议下，她开始使用大麻来缓解头痛。

sentences.en: And at first, it was phenomenal.
sentences.zh: 起初，效果好得惊人。

sentences.en: I could, you know, take a couple of hits or take an edible and the migraine was gone.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我只要抽上几口或者吃点大麻制品，偏头痛就消失了。

sentences.en: And I thought, this is fantastic.
sentences.zh: 我当时觉得，这太棒了。

sentences.en: Well, I don't have to take all these pills anymore and all this stuff.
sentences.zh: 我再也不用吃那些乱七八糟的药了。

sentences.en: And Jennifer found that using marijuana medically really helped her with her health problem.
sentences.zh: 詹妮弗发现，医用大麻确实对她的健康问题很有帮助。

sentences.en: She was using a couple times a week and that was enough.
sentences.zh: 她每周只用几次，这就足够了。

sentences.en: It solved the issue right away.
sentences.zh: 问题立刻就解决了。

sentences.en: And then...
sentences.zh: 然后……

sentences.en: About six months into it, I started getting stomach aches.
sentences.zh: 大约六个月后，我开始胃痛。

sentences.en: She starts to experience some nausea.
sentences.zh: 她开始出现一些恶心症状。

sentences.en: I started waking up nauseous every single morning.
sentences.zh: 我每天早上醒来都感到恶心。

sentences.en: I just was dry heaving and sometimes I would vomit and it just was...
sentences.zh: 我只是干呕，有时还会呕吐，那种感觉……

sentences.en: And an employee at the marijuana dispensary that she used advised her to increase her marijuana use.
sentences.zh: 她去的那家大麻药房的一名员工建议她增加大麻的使用量。

sentences.en: I would say, we have really good luck with this one because it's what we give chemo patients.
sentences.zh: 我会说，这种产品效果很好，因为我们给化疗病人用的就是这个。

sentences.en: And I'd say, all right, give it to me, you know.
sentences.zh: 我就说，好吧，给我吧。

sentences.en: And eventually she was using the drug nearly every day.
sentences.zh: 最终，她几乎每天都在使用这种药物。

sentences.en: And it would help me and I would feel better and I was okay to eat.
sentences.zh: 它确实能帮我缓解，让我感觉好点，也能吃下东西。

sentences.en: And then, you know, it would wear off and then it was a cycle that just kept going and going.
sentences.zh: 但药效一过，这种循环就没完没了地持续下去。

sentences.en: But the nausea actually got worse.
sentences.zh: 但恶心的情况实际上变得更糟了。

sentences.en: She starts to get cycles of severe vomiting and stomach pain.
sentences.zh: 她开始出现严重的呕吐和胃痛周期。

sentences.en: I was pretty much bedridden.
sentences.zh: 我几乎卧床不起。

sentences.en: I mean, on a good day, I was just mildly nauseous.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，状态好的时候，也只是轻微恶心。

sentences.en: On a bad day, I was, you know, on the bathroom floor crying my eyes out.
sentences.zh: 状态不好的时候，我就只能躺在浴室地板上哭得撕心裂肺。

sentences.en: You know, just totally desperate for help.
sentences.zh: 你知道，就是那种极度渴望得到帮助的感觉。

sentences.en: And it just went on and on and on.
sentences.zh: 这种情况一直持续不断。

sentences.en: She was often in immense pain and it was really scary to her.
sentences.zh: 她经常处于剧痛之中，这让她感到非常害怕。

sentences.en: But when she sought medical attention, you know, they had no answers.
sentences.zh: 但当她寻求医疗帮助时，他们却束手无策。

sentences.en: They said, well...
sentences.zh: 他们说，嗯……

sentences.en: Doctor after doctor could not figure out what was wrong with her.
sentences.zh: 医生换了一个又一个，都查不出她到底出了什么毛病。

sentences.en: Then they started doing CAT scans and stomach tests and, I mean, blood tests and all these workups.
sentences.zh: 接着他们开始做CT扫描、胃部检查，还有验血，做了各种检查。

sentences.en: And, you know, you name it, I had it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你能想到的检查我都做过了。

sentences.en: Over the course of three years, I went to 12 different doctors.
sentences.zh: 在三年时间里，我看了12位不同的医生。

sentences.en: I went to, including four different gastroenterologists.
sentences.zh: 我看了包括四位不同的胃肠科医生。

sentences.en: I went to neurologists.
sentences.zh: 我看了神经科医生。

sentences.en: I went to internists.
sentences.zh: 我看了内科医生。

sentences.en: I went to functional medicine doctors.
sentences.zh: 我看了功能医学医生。

sentences.en: I did acupuncture.
sentences.zh: 我试过针灸。

sentences.en: I did restriction diets.
sentences.zh: 我试过限制饮食。

sentences.en: I gave up, you know, every food group forever.
sentences.zh: 我放弃了所有种类的食物，永远地。

sentences.en: And I just kept getting sicker and sicker and sicker.
sentences.zh: 但我却变得越来越虚弱。

sentences.en: She gets all of these different diagnoses.
sentences.zh: 她得到了各种各样的诊断结果。

sentences.en: At one point, she actually has her gallbladder removed.
sentences.zh: 有一次，她甚至切除了胆囊。

sentences.en: Oh, my God.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: And it was really discouraging because nothing was helping.
sentences.zh: 这真的很令人沮丧，因为什么方法都没用。

sentences.en: I really had some very dark days where I thought, you know, I'm going to die.
sentences.zh: 我确实经历过非常黑暗的日子，当时我想，我要死了。

sentences.en: I'm, because this is it for me.
sentences.zh: 因为我的人生到头了。

sentences.en: I can't get out of bed, you know.
sentences.zh: 我连床都下不了。

sentences.en: And no one seems to know what to do.
sentences.zh: 而且似乎没人知道该怎么办。

sentences.en: And I don't, you know, this is it.
sentences.zh: 我不知道，这就是终点。

sentences.en: Then one day...
sentences.zh: 直到有一天……

sentences.en: June 16th, 2022.
I will remember the day.
sentences.zh: 我会记住这一天。

sentences.en: She's once again on the internet trying to find any possible cause for this pain that she's in.
sentences.zh: 她再次上网，试图找出这种疼痛的任何可能原因。

sentences.en: And, you know, way down on the Google search pages, I saw a link to the Facebook page.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在谷歌搜索页面的很后面，我看到了一个指向Facebook页面的链接。

sentences.en: And she finds this Facebook group that is made up of people who are suffering from a condition called cannabinoid hyperemesis syndrome, known as CHS.
sentences.zh: 她找到了这个Facebook群组，里面都是患有一种叫“大麻素剧吐综合征”（简称CHS）的人。

sentences.en: And it's the first time she has any inkling that the weed might be causing her pain.
sentences.zh: 这是她第一次意识到，大麻可能就是导致她痛苦的原因。

sentences.en: And what exactly is CHS?
sentences.zh: 那么，到底什么是CHS？

sentences.en: Well, it's really interesting, right?
sentences.zh: 这真的很有趣，对吧？

sentences.en: Because marijuana is widely known for helping with nausea.
sentences.zh: 因为大麻以缓解恶心而广为人知。

sentences.en: But in some cases, with certain chronic users, it can actually have the opposite effect.
sentences.zh: 但在某些情况下，对于某些长期使用者来说，它实际上会产生相反的效果。

sentences.en: We're talking about really severe nausea, severe vomiting, cycles of severe vomiting,
sentences.zh: 我们指的是非常严重的恶心、剧烈呕吐，以及严重的呕吐周期，

sentences.en: in which people are in so much pain that they actually use the term scrommeting because they're often screaming out in pain.
sentences.zh: 人们痛苦到甚至用“尖叫呕吐”（scrommeting）这个词，因为他们经常痛得大声尖叫。

sentences.en: It's so awful.
sentences.zh: 太可怕了。

sentences.en: Oh, my God.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And this is a relatively new syndrome.
sentences.zh: 这是一种相对较新的综合征。

sentences.en: It was first identified in 2004.
sentences.zh: 它最早在2004年被发现。

sentences.en: And basically, it's rise, like completely tracks with the rise in legalization and commercialization and the change in these products.
sentences.zh: 基本上，它的发病率完全随着大麻合法化、商业化以及产品形态的变化而上升。

sentences.en: And it's still quite a mystery.
sentences.zh: 而且它仍然是一个谜。

sentences.en: They don't know why some chronic users get it and others don't.
sentences.zh: 他们不知道为什么有些长期使用者会得这种病，而其他人却不会。

sentences.en: And there's also this telltale sign to the syndrome that is also not understood.
sentences.zh: 这种综合征还有一个明显的特征，目前也尚未被理解。

sentences.en: And that's that hot water often relieves symptoMs.
sentences.zh: 那就是热水通常能缓解症状。

sentences.en: So people who develop the syndrome will often spend hour after hour in really, really hot baths or showers, sometimes to the point where they burn themselves.
sentences.zh: 所以患有这种综合征的人经常会花上几个小时泡在非常非常热的浴缸或淋浴下，有时甚至会烫伤自己。

sentences.en: And the cases can be really severe.
sentences.zh: 病例可能非常严重。

sentences.en: It can lead to extreme dehydration, seizures, kidney failure, and even cardiac arreSt.
sentences.zh: 它会导致极度脱水、癫痫、肾衰竭，甚至心脏骤停。

sentences.en: We found eight deaths linked to CHS.
sentences.zh: 我们发现了八起与CHS有关的死亡案例。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: How common is this syndrome?
sentences.zh: 这种综合征有多普遍？

sentences.en: It's hard to say with certainty just how many people are suffering from CHS at this point.
sentences.zh: 目前很难确定到底有多少人患有CHS。

sentences.en: You know, even 20 years after it was first identified, there's not a single diagnostic code for it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，即使在它被发现20年后，医学上仍然没有统一的诊断代码。

sentences.en: So there's no uniform tracking of it in the medical system.
sentences.zh: 所以医疗系统中没有统一的追踪记录。

sentences.en: But what we heard from our interviews and surveys of doctors is that they're seeing more and more of it.
sentences.zh: 但我们从采访和医生调查中了解到，他们看到的情况越来越多。

sentences.en: And many described it now as a common thing that is presenting in emergency departments.
sentences.zh: 许多人现在将其描述为急诊室中常见的一种病症。

sentences.en: One doctor referred to it as a bread-and-butter diagnostic.
sentences.zh: 一位医生称其为“家常便饭”般的诊断。

sentences.en: Others said they see it every week, if not every day.
sentences.zh: 其他人则表示，他们每周甚至每天都能见到。

sentences.en: And there are also researchers who have estimated that as many as 30 percent of heavy users, regular users, of marijuana, are experiencing some symptoms of the syndrome.
sentences.zh: 还有研究人员估计，多达30%的大麻重度使用者或常客正在经历该综合征的某些症状。

sentences.en: So that would mean an estimated 6 million people.
sentences.zh: 这意味着估计有600万人。

sentences.en: And Jennifer is one of those people, correct?
sentences.zh: 詹妮弗就是其中之一，对吧？

sentences.en: What happened to her?
sentences.zh: 她后来怎么样了？

sentences.en: So after finding the Facebook group and realizing what's going on...
sentences.zh: 在找到那个Facebook群组并意识到发生了什么之后……

sentences.en: You know, I had taken my last edible at 9 o'clock that morning, and this was at 9.30 when I found the page.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那天早上9点我刚吃了最后一份大麻制品，9点半我就发现了那个页面。

sentences.en: I said, that's it, I'm done.
sentences.zh: 我说，够了，我受够了。

sentences.en: There's even a tiny, tiny, minuscule chance that this is it.
sentences.zh: 哪怕只有万分之一的可能，这就是原因所在。

sentences.en: You know, I'm done.
sentences.zh: 我决定戒了。

sentences.en: Let's see what happens.
sentences.zh: 看看会发生什么。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: She decides to quit marijuana on the spot.
sentences.zh: 她当场决定戒掉大麻。

sentences.en: And that leads to a period of withdrawal that lasts for about two months.
sentences.zh: 这导致了一段持续约两个月的戒断期。

sentences.en: And I just got better and better from then.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，我的情况就越来越好。

sentences.en: And, I mean, it's been two years, and I'm fine.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，已经过去两年了，我很好。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And after that, she's been totally fine.
sentences.zh: 在那之后，她一直完全正常。

sentences.en: That is, that is wild.
sentences.zh: 这真是太不可思议了。

sentences.en: I mean...
sentences.zh: 我的意思是……

sentences.en: It's wild.
sentences.zh: 太疯狂了。

sentences.en: And during this period of withdrawal,
sentences.zh: 在戒断期间，

sentences.en: she sees yet another specialist who confirms that she did indeed have CHS and actually told Jennifer that she was seeing multiple cases of the syndrome every week.
sentences.zh: 她又看了一位专家，对方证实她确实患有CHS，并告诉詹妮弗，他每周都能见到好几例这样的病例。

sentences.en: You mentioned before that there were several potential marijuana-related health issues you were looking into with those surveys.
sentences.zh: 你之前提到，你在那些调查中研究了几个潜在的大麻相关健康问题。

sentences.en: What else did you find?
sentences.zh: 你还发现了什么？

sentences.en: So, another significant harm that we identified that is very concerning is the relationship between marijuana and psychosis.
sentences.zh: 我们发现的另一个非常令人担忧的重大危害是大麻与精神病之间的关系。

sentences.en: And one of the ways that that plays out is marijuana causing a temporary psychotic episode or symptoms, paranoia, hallucinations.
sentences.zh: 其中一种表现是大麻导致短暂的精神病发作或症状，如偏执、幻觉。

sentences.en: And that can happen to all different kinds of people, people of different ages, chronic users of marijuana or first-time users of marijuana,
sentences.zh: 这种情况可能发生在各种人身上，不同年龄段的人，长期使用者或初次使用者，

sentences.en: people who are otherwise at risk for experiencing psychosis or have no other risk factors at all.
sentences.zh: 无论他们原本是否有患精神病的风险，还是完全没有其他风险因素。

sentences.en: And, you know, one of the people that I spoke to who had experienced this is a man named Javante Hill who lives in Colorado and tried marijuana at the suggestion of his girlfriend.
sentences.zh: 我采访过的一位经历过这种情况的人叫贾万特·希尔（Javante Hill），他住在科罗拉多州，在女友的建议下尝试了大麻。

sentences.en: You know, I'm not like a...
sentences.zh: 你知道，我不是那种……

sentences.en: He was a recent Navy veteran with PTSD, anxiety, and depression, and his girlfriend was an occasional marijuana user and told him that it could be a nice way to chill out.
sentences.zh: 他是一位刚退伍的海军老兵，患有创伤后应激障碍（PTSD）、焦虑症和抑郁症，他的女友偶尔使用大麻，告诉他这是一种放松的好方法。

sentences.en: So, one night, and this was just his second time using it, he took a bong hit and ended up totally paranoid and hallucinating.
sentences.zh: 所以有一天晚上，这只是他第二次使用，他抽了一口水烟筒，结果变得极度偏执并产生了幻觉。

sentences.en: And slowly, surely, as the night went on, I completely lost all touch with reality, and I replayed a lot of my...
sentences.zh: 随着夜晚的推移，我慢慢地完全失去了与现实的联系，我重温了许多……

sentences.en: Like, it's almost like all my worst fears came to the forefront, and I was seeing depictions of the devil and hell and just, like, literal demons, I thought were, like,
sentences.zh: 就像我内心深处最恐惧的事情全都涌现了出来，我看到了魔鬼和地狱的景象，还有真正的恶魔，我以为它们是……

sentences.en: in real life.
sentences.zh: 在现实生活中。

sentences.en: He said it was like he was in hell with devils.
sentences.zh: 他说感觉就像身处地狱，周围都是魔鬼。

sentences.en: Oh, my God.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: His girlfriend, Eva Zamora, who I also spoke with, was there trying to comfort him, but he didn't recognize her.
sentences.zh: 我也采访了他的女友伊娃·萨莫拉（Eva Zamora），她当时在场试图安慰他，但他认不出她了。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And in the midst of this, their dogs started fighting.
sentences.zh: 就在这时，他们的狗打了起来。

sentences.en: And then he had gone upstairs, and he came downstairs, and he...
sentences.zh: 然后他上楼去了，又下楼来，他……

sentences.en: He ended up getting his gun.
sentences.zh: 他最终拿到了枪。

sentences.en: The best way I can explain it is, like, I was looking at him, and, like, he was looking past me.
sentences.zh: 我能解释的最好方式是，我看着他，而他却看向我身后。

sentences.en: And he looked like he was scared.
sentences.zh: 他看起来很害怕。

sentences.en: Had the gun up, and he took...
sentences.zh: 他举起枪，然后……

sentences.en: Shooting and killing one of the dogs.
sentences.zh: 开枪打死了一只狗。

sentences.en: Ugh.
sentences.zh: 呃。

sentences.en: And actually shooting and injuring his girlfriend, Eva.
sentences.zh: 还开枪打伤了他的女友伊娃。

sentences.en: It was very dramatic.
sentences.zh: 这太戏剧性了。

sentences.en: Yeah, it was horrible.
sentences.zh: 是的，太可怕了。

sentences.en: He had no idea that this was a risk or even a possibility when he tried that marijuana.
sentences.zh: 他在尝试大麻时，根本不知道这是一种风险，甚至连可能性都没想过。

sentences.en: Nothing like this had ever happened to him before.
sentences.zh: 他以前从未发生过类似的事情。

sentences.en: You know, he had no history of psychosis.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他没有精神病史。

sentences.en: He had no history of domestic violence.
sentences.zh: 他也没有家庭暴力史。

sentences.en: After the incident, he was diagnosed with drug-induced hallucinations, and he ended up pleading guilty to animal cruelty and assault charges.
sentences.zh: 事件发生后，他被诊断为药物诱发的幻觉，最终对虐待动物和袭击指控认罪。

sentences.en: And he's actually suing the dispensary chain, claiming it failed to warn him about the risk of psychosis.
sentences.zh: 他实际上正在起诉那家药房连锁店，声称他们未能就精神错乱的风险向他发出警告。

sentences.en: And that type of temporary psychosis caused by marijuana is something that doctors are seeing across the country.
sentences.zh: 而这种由大麻引起的暂时性精神错乱，是医生们在全国各地都能看到的现象。

sentences.en: In our interviews and in our surveys of doctors, they said that they were seeing more and more patients with those kind of experiences.
sentences.zh: 在我们的采访和对医生的调查中，他们表示，他们看到的有此类经历的患者越来越多。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And you said that that kind of psychosis was temporary, but are there any other longer-term mental health implications?
sentences.zh: 你提到那种精神错乱是暂时性的，但还有其他长期的心理健康影响吗？

sentences.en: So marijuana can affect brain development, particularly during the critical period of adolescence, which actually goes up through age 25.
sentences.zh: 大麻会影响大脑发育，特别是在青春期这一关键时期，而这一时期实际上会持续到25岁。

sentences.en: And this is also the period when chronic psychotic disorders, like schizophrenia, typically emerge.
sentences.zh: 这也是慢性精神障碍（如精神分裂症）通常出现的时期。

sentences.en: And there's growing evidence that marijuana use can contribute to the development of those psychotic disorders.
sentences.zh: 越来越多的证据表明，使用大麻可能会导致这些精神障碍的产生。

sentences.en: Recent studies showed that the more potent the cannabis, the more frequent the use, and the earlier the age of consuming, the greater the risk.
sentences.zh: 最近的研究表明，大麻的效力越强、使用频率越高、开始使用的年龄越小，风险就越大。

sentences.en: And to be clear, this isn't like a clear-cut, black-and-white, cause-and-effect relationship between marijuana and chronic psychotic disorders.
sentences.zh: 需要明确的是，大麻与慢性精神障碍之间并非存在一种明确的、非黑即白的因果关系。

sentences.en: One researcher that I talked to, a professor at Yale University, who's paid a lot of attention to this issue, actually compared it to cigarette smoking and lung cancer.
sentences.zh: 我采访过的一位耶鲁大学教授非常关注这个问题，他实际上将其比作吸烟与肺癌的关系。

sentences.en: You know, not everybody who smokes cigarettes gets lung cancer.
sentences.zh: 你知道，并不是每个吸烟的人都会得肺癌。

sentences.en: Not everybody who has lung cancer smokes cigarettes.
sentences.zh: 也不是每个患有肺癌的人都吸烟。

sentences.en: But we know after decades that there's a strong association between the two.
sentences.zh: 但经过几十年的研究，我们知道两者之间存在强烈的关联。

sentences.en: And as he put it, the same goes for marijuana use and these chronic psychotic disorders.
sentences.zh: 正如他所言，大麻的使用与这些慢性精神障碍之间也是如此。

sentences.en: And doctors told us that they are seeing more and more of these chronic psychotic disorders in which they believe cannabis played a role.
sentences.zh: 医生们告诉我们，他们看到的这些他们认为与大麻有关的慢性精神障碍病例越来越多。

sentences.en: You know, Megan, we've talked about a few of these potentially awful side effects from marijuana use, like addiction, the bouts of vomiting,
sentences.zh: 梅根，我们讨论了一些大麻使用带来的潜在可怕副作用，比如成瘾、呕吐发作，

sentences.en: psychosis, and just longer-term mental health effects.
sentences.zh: 精神错乱，以及更长期的心理健康影响。

sentences.en: And what strikes me is that all of this stuff really runs counter to the narrative that I imagine a lot of people have about marijuana, which is that it's relatively safe.
sentences.zh: 让我感到震惊的是，所有这些都与我想象中许多人对大麻的看法背道而驰，即认为它相对安全。

sentences.en: Yeah, listen, our public understanding of this drug hasn't kept pace with the transformation of it and this new commercial industry and these shifts in how people are using it.
sentences.zh: 是的，听着，公众对这种药物的理解并没有跟上它的转变、新的商业产业以及人们使用方式的变化。

sentences.en: And I know, at least from many of the people who have experienced harms from marijuana, some of these harms that we've discussed, that when they tried to talk about it,
sentences.zh: 我知道，至少从许多经历过大麻危害的人那里，也就是我们讨论过的一些危害，当他们试图谈论这些时，

sentences.en: they often ran into not just skepticism, but also sometimes downright hostility.
sentences.zh: 他们往往不仅会遇到怀疑，有时甚至会遇到彻底的敌意。

sentences.en: Yeah, actually, you're reminding me, I noticed that when The Times posted your story on Instagram, there was this comment from the comedian Eric Andre, and he said something like,
sentences.zh: 是的，你提醒了我，我注意到当《泰晤士报》在Instagram上发布你的报道时，喜剧演员埃里克·安德烈评论说，

sentences.en: whose side are you on?
sentences.zh: 你站在哪一边？

sentences.en: And it made me wonder how broadly you felt that sentiment.
sentences.zh: 这让我好奇你感受到的这种情绪有多普遍。

sentences.en: Like, after all this work to increase access to marijuana, were people not receptive to hearing that it might be bad for you?
sentences.zh: 比如，在为增加大麻获取渠道做了这么多工作之后，人们是否不愿听到它可能对你有害？

sentences.en: You know, I actually saw that comment as well, Rachel, that caught my eye.
sentences.zh: 瑞秋，其实我也看到了那条评论，它引起了我的注意。

sentences.en: But I want to be very clear about what else we found in our reporting, which is that the majority of the doctors that we talked to support the legalization of marijuana.
sentences.zh: 但我想要非常明确地说明我们在报道中还发现了什么，那就是我们采访的大多数医生都支持大麻合法化。

sentences.en: Even the majority of people that we interviewed and surveyed who had been harmed by marijuana, none of them were saying, like, this is categorically a bad drug
sentences.zh: 即使是我们采访和调查的大多数受过大麻伤害的人，也没有人说这是一种绝对糟糕的药物，

sentences.en: and should not be made available.
sentences.zh: 或者不应该提供给公众。

sentences.en: What we heard time and again is that the way that legalization and commercialization is playing out in this country is flawed.
sentences.zh: 我们反复听到的是，这个国家目前合法化和商业化的方式是有缺陷的。

sentences.en: That the government and the medical system need to be doing more to track the health effects of marijuana.
sentences.zh: 政府和医疗系统需要做更多的工作来追踪大麻对健康的影响。

sentences.en: They need to be doing more to document that.
sentences.zh: 他们需要做更多的工作来记录这些影响。

sentences.en: And they need to also be communicating that to consumers.
sentences.zh: 而且他们还需要将这些信息传达给消费者。

sentences.en: That these consumers have a right to know about the associations with psychosis.
sentences.zh: 消费者有权了解它与精神错乱之间的关联。

sentences.en: They have a right to know about the risk of this becoming addictive.
sentences.zh: 他们有权了解这种药物成瘾的风险。

sentences.en: They have the right to know about CHS.
sentences.zh: 他们有权了解大麻素剧吐综合征（CHS）。

sentences.en: You know, Jennifer Macaluso, for example, said, if I had known that CHS existed, if that had been on a warning label, I wouldn't have increased my use of the drug
sentences.zh: 例如，詹妮弗·马卡卢索说，如果我早知道有CHS，如果警告标签上有写，我就不会在开始出现症状时，

sentences.en: when I started experiencing symptoMs.
sentences.zh: 还增加药物的使用量了。

sentences.en: And so I think that the uniform message that came out of this reporting was there needs to be better oversight there needs to be better protections
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这份报道传达出的统一信息是：需要更好的监管，需要更好的保护，

sentences.en: and there needs to be better information.
sentences.zh: 并且需要更好的信息披露。

sentences.en: Megan, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 梅根，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你邀请我。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: I'm grateful to be back here in Lebanon, but I have to admit that I'm saddened to bear witness to the pain of its people
sentences.zh: 我很感激能回到黎巴嫩，但我必须承认，目睹这里人民的痛苦，

sentences.en: and what they're experiencing.
sentences.zh: 以及他们正在经历的一切，我感到非常难过。

sentences.en: In Lebanon on Monday, a top U.S.
sentences.zh: 周一在黎巴嫩，一位美国高级官员表示，

sentences.en: official said that the growing conflict between Israel and Hezbollah has spun out of control, and he outlined a proposal to bring it to an end.
sentences.zh: 以色列和真主党之间日益加剧的冲突已经失控，他概述了一项结束冲突的提议。

sentences.en: And I want to be very, very clear.
sentences.zh: 我想非常、非常明确地说明一点。

sentences.en: Tying Lebanon's future
sentences.zh: 将黎巴嫩的未来

sentences.en: to other conflicts in the region
sentences.zh: 与该地区的其他冲突挂钩，

sentences.en: was not and is not in the interest of the Lebanese people.
sentences.zh: 过去不是，现在也不是黎巴嫩人民的利益所在。

sentences.en: The official, the American diplomat Amos Hochstein, called on both sides to abide by a U.N.
sentences.zh: 这位官员，美国外交官阿莫斯·霍克斯坦，呼吁双方遵守联合国

sentences.en: resolution reached back in 2006 that would require Israel to withdraw its troops from Lebanon and for Hezbollah to be disarmed along Lebanon's border with Israel.
sentences.zh: 在2006年达成的决议，该决议要求以色列从黎巴嫩撤军，并要求真主党在黎巴嫩与以色列边境解除武装。

sentences.en: Israel's recent military operations against Hezbollah, the Iranian-backed group that has launched thousands of rockets into Israel, has caused a humanitarian crisis in Lebanon
sentences.zh: 以色列最近针对真主党的军事行动——该组织是伊朗支持的，曾向以色列发射了数千枚火箭弹——在黎巴嫩造成了人道主义危机，

sentences.en: that has displaced about a fifth of the country's population.
sentences.zh: 导致该国约五分之一的人口流离失所。

sentences.zh: 今天的节目由威尔·里德制作，

sentences.zh: 亚历克斯·斯特恩和奥利维亚·纳普参与制作。

sentences.zh: 由迈克·贝努瓦编辑，马克·乔治提供协助。

sentences.zh: 包含原创音乐，由

sentences.zh: 由克里斯·伍德进行工程处理。

sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由Wonderly的吉姆·布伦伯格和本·兰兹伯格创作。

sentences.zh: 以上就是《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Rachel AbraMs.
sentences.zh: 我是瑞秋·艾布拉姆斯。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直像一台受到严密控制的机器一样运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 选举迎来了一群自称改革派的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直陷入一场伤痕累累、混乱不堪，有时又令人兴奋的斗争中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在《Metro》的最新一期节目中，我和萨拉·凯尼格将讲述人们试图维持影响力却在过程中失去控制的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《Metro》。

sentences.zh: 在任何你获取播客的地方收听。
